speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad
text: asked the Minister for Education what efforts are being undertaken to educate our educators and lecturers in our institutes of higher learning (IHLs) so that they are aware of (i) the effects of COVID-19, (ii) efforts undertaken by the Government to manage the developing situation and (iii) the part they can play in social defence by calming any unnecessary panic that may arise among our IHL students.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Government efforts to manage the outbreak in Singapore as well as the precautionary measures taken are explained to the communities in these IHLs.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: They are doing this through various advisories and resources.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Beyond technical knowledge, the COVID-19 situation is also a teachable moment to build resilience.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: The universities will incorporate similar lessons where opportune.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: It will incorporate insights from the ongoing COVID-19 situation.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Many students and staff are also stepping forward with help and moral support.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: In the universities, student groups have rallied to provide support and daily food deliveries for their peers living on campus but are required to stay in their rooms.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: In our polytechnics, staff from our nursing schools help to train their colleagues in conducting temperature screening.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: These ground initiatives and actions are contagious, demonstrate the courage of the Singapore society and have more educational value than many formal courses.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We should build on these positive initiatives to build a more resilient and cohesive Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Together, I am confident we can overcome this COVID-19 episode.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: Very heartening to hear such initiatives taking place.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: From my understanding, there are several IHLs which have cancelled classes or switched to e-learning.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: However, some classes are still happening and going on as per normal.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: What is the guidance from the Ministry of Education that has been given to all the IHLs in terms of cancellation of classes or postponement of massive events?

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: The second supplementary question is: when can we see us easing back to normalising the situation?

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: So, you find lectures are still ongoing but they have shrank in size.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: It was fortunate many of them were not in campus when they had symptoms.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: They exercised responsibility, which was fortunate, and we are very thankful to them.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: As a result, the number of staff and students that have to be quarantined or put on Leave of Absence has been much reduced.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: I think they are all stable, improving and we are glad.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: We hope to see them back in school soon.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: As to when it will stabilise, it really depends on the situation.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: I think we have to ask Minister Gan Kim Yong on this.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: But we will play our part and do our best to make sure that within schools, while we educate the students, we take the necessary precautions so that life can go on and education can go on as normally as we can, but with precautions.
